scenes.narration: Every AI starts out terrible. Practice fixes that.
Welcome to FredsDesk, lesson five. In under a minute, you'll see how an AI gets better through practice.
Learning means adjusting. The AI makes a guess, checks how wrong it was, and tweaks its settings to be a little less wrong next time.
scenes.definition: Guess, measure the mistake, adjust, repeat.

scenes.narration: Think of a basketball player at the free-throw line. She shoots, sees how far she missed, and adjusts her aim. A thousand shots later, the ball drops in almost every time.
An AI does the same, with numbers. It predicts an answer. A score called the loss measures the error. Then training nudges the weights to shrink it. And the loop repeats, over and over.
No one hands it the rule. After millions of tiny nudges, the pattern simply emerges.
scenes.label: Millions of them add up to skill
scenes.sub: The pattern emerges on its own.

scenes.narration: Quick recap. One: learning is guess, check, adjust. Two: the loss measures how wrong the guess was. Three: millions of small nudges add up.
points: Millions of small nudges add up

scenes.narration: Quiz time! When an AI makes a mistake in training, does it A, adjust its weights, or B, erase its memory? Answer in the comments. Tomorrow: what is an LLM? Follow FredsDesk, and see you at the desk.
scenes.question: When an AI makes a mistake in training, what happens?

post.title: How does an AI learn? Guess, check, adjust | AI Lesson #5
post.description: Lesson 5 of FredsDesk's daily AI series: how an AI improves through a loop of guessing, measuring error and nudging its weights. Quiz inside!
post.pinned_comment: Quiz answer: A. Training measures the mistake and nudges the weights to shrink it; nothing gets erased. What did you pick? 👇
